transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

I'm mainly here because my sleep has gotten really unreliable lately. Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there replaying sales forecasts and team issues from work. And then, if I do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's really starting to wear me out.
Outside of your sleep, would you say that you find yourself worrying excessively about a wide range of different topics or events in your daily life?

Yeah, I definitely do. Most days, my mind just kind of jumps from one thing to another. I'll start off worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. Then it shifts to personal stuff like the mortgage, or back to work with a client renewal. It just feels like every small delay could turn into something major.
Beyond the worry and sleep issues, have you noticed that you are no longer finding pleasure or interest in the activities that you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still enjoy the things I usually like to do. Sometimes I'm just too exhausted to actually do them because of how little sleep I'm getting, but... no, when I do have free time or see my friends, I still have fun. It's really just the constant worrying and the lack of sleep that are the main problems.
Do you often feel physically tense, such as having tight muscles, aches, or feeling like you can't sit still?

Yeah, actually. I feel wound up almost all the time. It's like... I feel like I'm sitting in a high-pressure pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And my muscles definitely feel it. My shoulders just stay tight, no matter how much I try to relax them.
How long have you been experiencing this persistent pattern of worry and physical tension?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say this has been building since the sales division reorganization... so that was about thirteen months ago. Yeah, a little over a year.
Do you find that your mind frequently goes blank or that you have difficulty concentrating on tasks because of these worries?

No, I haven't really noticed that. My mind doesn't go blank... if anything, it's the opposite. It's just constantly running through all the things I'm worried about. I can still focus on my work when I need to, it just takes more effort sometimes because I'm so tired. But no, I wouldn't say I have trouble concentrating or my mind going blank.
Do you find that you have become more irritable or easily annoyed with others since this started?

Yeah, I have, actually. I've noticed I've started snapping at my reps at work over really minor things, like... just small CRM updates that shouldn't be a big deal. And it happens at home, too. I'll get annoyed at my husband over little things, like a few dishes left in the sink. Afterward, I always know my reaction was way bigger than the situation actually warranted, but... yeah, I definitely get irritated more easily now.
